Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Thawri, Abu Salih and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Spread it out﴾ means extended it.

* *

﴿And a soul and He who proportioned it﴾, meaning: He created it proportioned, upright, upon the sound natural disposition (fitrah), as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind; there is no change in the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30]. * *

Ahmad and Muslim related it, from the hadith of 'Azrah ibn Thabit with this chain. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/135), al-Musnad (4/438), and Sahih Muslim no. (2650).]]

* *

﴿He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it﴾. Imam Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, from Nafi' (from Ibn 'Umar), from Salih ibn Sa'id, from 'A'ishah, that she missed the Prophet ﷺ from his bed, so she touched him with her hand, and her hand fell upon him while he was prostrating, and he was saying: "My Lord, give my soul its righteousness, and purify it; You are the best of those who purify it, You are its Guardian and its Master." [[Al-Musnad (6/209).]] He alone related it.

O Allah, give my soul its righteousness, and purify it; You are the best of those who purify it, You are its Guardian and its Master. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a heart that does not humble itself, from a soul that is never satisfied, from knowledge that does not benefit, and from a supplication that is not answered." Zayd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us these, and we would teach them to you.

Muslim related it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith and Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Zayd ibn Arqam, with it. [[Al-Musnad (4/371) and Sahih Muslim no. (2722).]]

Ibn Kathir says that Allah informs about Thamud, that they denied their Messenger because of their transgression and rebellion.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿بِطَغْوَاهَا﴾ means "with all of it" (i.e., with their entire people).

The first view is more correct, as stated by Mujahid, Qatadah and others. So that resulted in their denial in their hearts of the guidance and certainty that their Messenger brought them.

﴿إِذِ انْبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا﴾ means the most wretched of the tribe, who was Qudar ibn Salif, the slayer of the she-camel, and he was the "little reddish one" of Thamud. He is the one Allah refers to when He says: ﴿They called their companion, and he took (the sword) and hamstrung (her)﴾ [Al-Qamar: 29]. This man was powerful among them, honored in his people, of noble lineage, a leader who was obeyed, as Imam Ahmad said:

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Zam'ah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon, mentioning the she-camel and the one who hamstrung her, and he said: "﴿When the most wretched of them was sent forth﴾; he was sent forth against her as a man, mighty, powerful and protected within his clan, like Abu Zam'ah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Yazid ibn Muhammad ibn Khutham narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Muhammad ibn Khutham Abu Yazid, from Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ali: "Shall I inform you of the most wretched of people?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Two men: the little reddish one of Thamud, who hamstrung the she-camel, and the one who will strike you, O Ali, on this [and he indicated his horn/crown of the head] until this [beard] becomes wet with it," meaning his beard.

* *

His words: ﴿Then the Messenger of Allah said to them﴾, meaning Salih, peace be upon him: ﴿the she-camel of Allah﴾, i.e., beware of harming the she-camel of Allah, ﴿and her drink﴾, i.e., do not transgress against her water, for she has a day's drink and you have a known day's drink. Allah said: ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her﴾, i.e., they denied him in what he brought them, so that resulted in them hamstringing the she-camel that Allah had brought out of the rock as a sign for them and a proof against them. ﴿So their Lord destroyed them for their sin﴾, i.e., He became angry with them and destroyed them, ﴿and leveled them﴾, i.e., He made the punishment descend upon them equally.

Qatadah said: We have been told that the little reddish one of Thamud did not hamstring the she-camel until their small and great, their males and females, joined him. When the people shared in hamstringing her, Allah destroyed them for their sins and leveled them.

* *

His words: ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾. It is also recited: "fa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha".

Ibn Abbas said: Allah does not fear any retribution from anyone. Likewise said Mujahid, al-Hasan, Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, and others.

Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾, i.e., the one who hamstrung her did not fear the consequence of what he did. The first view is more correct, due to the indication of the context, and Allah knows best.

End of the tafsir of "Wash-shamsi wa duhaha."

His words: ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾. It is also recited: "fa-la yakhafu 'uqbaha".

Ibn Abbas said: Allah does not fear any retribution from anyone. Likewise said Mujahid, al-Hasan, Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, and others.

Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾, i.e., the one who hamstrung her did not fear the consequence of what he did. The first view is more correct, due to the indication of the context, and Allah knows best.

End of the tafsir of "Wash-shamsi wa duhaha."
